subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should maintainers keep this issue as the umbrella RFC for multi-session architecture, or supersede it with narrower product-approved trackers for routing, session UI, topic-session families, and shared memory?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose the permanent all-channel session model, config surface, storage migration, or public-memory privacy boundary because those choices affect core architecture and security posture.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split work
options.body: Use this issue for architecture coordination while moving accepted slices into focused session-routing, UI lifecycle, topic-family, and memory/security issues.

options.title: Supersede with narrower trackers
options.body: Close this umbrella after pointing users to the active narrower issues that preserve each remaining scope.

options.title: Decline broad core architecture
options.body: Reject the RFC as too broad for core unless maintainers first identify a missing plugin, session, or memory API gap.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split work
recommendation.body: Use this issue for architecture coordination while moving accepted slices into focused session-routing, UI lifecycle, topic-family, and memory/security issues.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from issue mentions, related product-tracker discussion, and recent session/UI/security history.
